title: EVFTA’s competitive advantage to not last forever: Vietnamese experts
content:
Though the EU-Vietnam FTA has played a key role in expanding Vietnam’s exports to the EU and helping businesses boost competitiveness, experts caution this advantage will not last indefinitely.
Vietnamese businesses are being urged to move beyond relying on tariff incentives and instead invest in technology, green transformation, data governance and traceability to maximise the FTA's long-term benefits.

title: UK's private sector activity outlook improves to -18%, CBI says
content:
UK private sector activity is expected to fall for the quarter to October, with CBI's indicator at -18 per cent, its least negative since March.
Textile, apparel and retail supply chains face weak demand signals, with manufacturing output at a -30 per cent balance.
Distribution sales are at a -20 per cent balance, while subdued demand, hesitant customers and cost pressures keep margins squeezed.

title: Bangladesh Bank cuts policy rate by 50 bps to 9.5%
content:
Bangladesh Bank has reduced the policy rate by 50 bps to 9.5 per cent to support growth, encourage private sector investment, improve credit flow and generate employment. 
The new rate will be effective from August 2. 
The bank’s monetary policy committee also lowered the standing lending facility rate by 50 bps to 11 per cent, while leaving the standing deposit facility rate unchanged at 7.5 per cent.

title: Vietnam, Cambodia to promote transport links, logistics cooperation
content:
Vietnam and Cambodia recently agreed to promote transport infrastructure connectivity, border gate development, logistics cooperation and supply chains; facilitate trade and investment; and work towards taking bilateral trade to $20 billion in the near future. 
Vietnamese National Assembly chairman and Cambodian National Assembly president pledged to accelerate border demarcation and marker planting.

title: Canada Goose reports higher Q1 sales, improved margins
content:
Canada Goose’s Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21 per cent to C$84.8 million (~$60.4 million); losses narrowed and gross margin reached 66.1 per cent. 
DTC sales grew 37 per cent on higher store and e-commerce traffic and conversions; wholesale fell 12 per cent as partner demand softened. 
The brand kept FY27 guidance at C$1.4–1.5 billion (~$997.5 million–$1.07 billion) and plans four to six DTC stores.

title: US’ Columbia Sportswear returns to profit in Q2, lifts FY26 outlook
content:
American manufacturer and distributor Columbia Sportswear Company has returned to profitability in Q2 FY26 as net sales rose 2 per cent to $614.4 million, supported by international growth and a $78 million IEEPA tariff refund. 
The company raised its FY26 profit and EPS guidance, while maintaining its sales outlook despite softer US demand and ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty.

title: Canada's Gildan Activewear's Q1 revenue surges 64% on HanesBrands deal
content:
Gildan Activewear Inc, a Canadian apparel manufacturer, posted record first-quarter net sales of $1.17 billion, rising 63.8 per cent YoY, driven by the full consolidation of HanesBrands. 
Despite the revenue jump, Gildan reported a net loss of $55.1 million from continuing operations and an operating margin of negative 0.1 per cent. 
Adjusted operating margin reached 14.3 per cent.
